title: Own a pharmacy business only as a pharmacist or another permitted owner
what: Only a pharmacist (or another person the Act allows) may own, or hold an interest in, a pharmacy business.

laws.title: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (South Australia) Act 2010 (SA)

sources.title: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (South Australia) Act 2010 (SA)
sources.quote: (1a) A person must not own, or hold a proprietary interest in, a pharmacy business unless that person is— (a) a pharmacist; or (b) a prescribed relative of a pharmacist who holds a proprietary interest in the pharmacy business; or (c) a recognised corporate pharmacy services provider; or (d) a recognised trustee pharmacy services provider; or (e) a partner in a partnership that carries on the business and in which every partner is either— (i) a pharmacist; or (ii) a prescribed relative of a partner who is a pharmacist; or (iii) a recognised corporate pharmacy services provider; or (iv) a recognised trustee pharmacy services provider. Maximum penalty: $50 000 or imprisonment for 6 months.

confidence_note: The Act's own words reserve ownership of pharmacy businesses to pharmacists and the providers it lists. Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the official text, which is not itself official.

assessment.summary: Only pharmacists may own pharmacies, and each may own only a few. It keeps other investors and business models out of community pharmacy; the Harper Review recommended removing the restriction.

marks.reason: Reserves ownership of pharmacies to pharmacists and caps how many each may own: an exclusive right to enter.

assessment.confidence_note: The restriction is explicit; its effect on prices and access has not been measured in Australia. Marks copied from the register item sa-pharmacy-ownership so the two agree.
